subject: maths
title: Decimals: Tenths and Hundredths
seo_title: Year 4 Decimals Worksheets: Tenths and Hundredths, Dividing by 10 and 100, Comparing and Rounding
standard_text: Count up and down in hundredths; recognise that hundredths arise when dividing an object by one hundred and dividing tenths by ten; recognise and write decimal equivalents of any number of tenths or hundredths; recognise and write decimal equivalents to 1/4, 1/2, 3/4; find the effect of dividing a one- or two-digit number by 10 and 100, identifying the value of the digits in the answer as ones, tenths and hundredths; round decimals with one decimal place to the nearest whole number; compare numbers with the same number of decimal places up to two decimal places.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 decimals worksheets for the National Curriculum: tenths and hundredths on a hundred square, 1/4 = 0.25, counting in hundredths, dividing by 10 and 100, comparing and rounding decimals, and money and measure problems. 100 maths questions with an answer key.
key_big: Tenths are the first place after the decimal point; hundredths are the second. 3/10 = 0.3 and 37/100 = 0.37.
key_sub: 1/4 = 0.25, 1/2 = 0.5, 3/4 = 0.75. Dividing by 10 moves the digits 1 place right, by 100 two places: 34 ÷ 100 = 0.34. Round with the tenths digit: 4.5 rounds up to 5.
body_html:
Tenths and hundredths

Divide 1 whole into 10 equal parts: each part is one tenth, 110 = 0.1. Divide it into 100 equal parts: each part is one hundredth, 1100 = 0.01. Dividing one tenth by 10 also gives one hundredth.

The first place after the decimal point is tenths. The second place is hundredths. Use a 0 to hold an empty place: 7100 = 0.07, not 0.7.

Halves and quarters as decimals

FractionHundredthsDecimal
14251000.25
12501000.5
34751000.75
Count in hundredths

Count on from 0.37 in hundredths.

0.37, 0.38, 0.39, then 10 hundredths make 1 tenth, so the next number is 0.40.

Answer: 0.38, 0.39, 0.40, 0.41

Dividing by 10 and 100

Dividing by 10 moves every digit 1 place to the right. Dividing by 100 moves every digit 2 places to the right. The decimal point stays where it is.

Example

7 ÷ 100

The 7 moves 2 places to the right, into the hundredths place. Put 0 in the ones and tenths places.

Answer: 0.07

Comparing and rounding

To compare decimals, look at the ones first, then the tenths, then the hundredths. 0.45 < 0.54, because 4 tenths < 5 tenths.

To round to the nearest whole number, look at the tenths digit. 5 or more: round up. 4 or less: round down.

Example

Round 4.5 to the nearest whole number.

4.5 is exactly halfway between 4 and 5. Halfway always rounds up.

Answer: 5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing 310 as 0.03Tenths use one place: 0.3
Writing 14 as 0.4 or 1.414 = 25100 = 0.25
34 ÷ 100 = 3.4÷ 100 moves digits 2 places: 0.34
Counting 0.38, 0.39, 0.31010 hundredths make 1 tenth: 0.39, 0.40
0.45 > 0.54 because 5 > 4 at the endCompare the tenths first: 4 < 5, so 0.45 < 0.54
Rounding 4.5 down to 4Halfway rounds up: 5

faq.q: What decimals do children learn in Year 4?
faq.a: In Year 4 children learn tenths and hundredths: they write decimals like 0.3 and 0.37, learn that 1/4 = 0.25, 1/2 = 0.5 and 3/4 = 0.75, divide one- and two-digit numbers by 10 and 100, compare decimals and round numbers like 4.6 to the nearest whole number.

faq.q: How do you explain hundredths to a child?
faq.a: Use a hundred square as 1 whole: each small square is one hundredth (0.01) and each column of 10 squares is one tenth (0.1). 37 shaded squares show 37 hundredths, which is 0.37.

faq.q: What happens when you divide a number by 10 or 100?
faq.a: Dividing by 10 moves every digit one place to the right, and dividing by 100 moves every digit two places to the right. So 34 ÷ 10 = 3.4 and 34 ÷ 100 = 0.34.

faq.q: How do you round a decimal to the nearest whole number?
faq.a: Look at the tenths digit. If it is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, round down. So 4.6 rounds to 5, 4.5 rounds to 5 and 4.3 rounds to 4.

items.q: The whole square is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth and each small square is 1 hundredth. 3 full columns and 7 squares are shaded: 3 tenths and 7 hundredths = 37100 = 0.37.

items.q: The whole square is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The hundred square has 100 equal squares, so each square is 1 hundredth. 8 squares are shaded and there is no full column, so there are 0 tenths. 8 hundredths = 8100 = 0.08. Write the 0 in the tenths place.

items.q: The whole square is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth and each small square is 1 hundredth. 5 full columns and 2 squares are shaded: 5 tenths and 2 hundredths = 52100 = 0.52.

items.q: The whole square is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth. 7 full columns are shaded: 7 tenths = 710 = 0.7 (or 0.70). 0.07 would be only 7 small squares.

items.q: The whole square is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth and each small square is 1 hundredth. 1 full column and 9 squares are shaded: 1 tenth and 9 hundredths = 19100 = 0.19.

items.q: The whole square is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The hundred square has 100 equal squares, so each square is 1 hundredth. 4 squares are shaded and there is no full column, so there are 0 tenths. 4 hundredths = 4100 = 0.04. Write the 0 in the tenths place.

items.q: The whole bar is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts, so each part is 1 tenth. 3 parts are shaded: 310 = 0.3. One digit after the decimal point means tenths.

items.q: The whole bar is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts, so each part is 1 tenth. 8 parts are shaded: 810 = 0.8. One digit after the decimal point means tenths.

items.q: Write 310 as a decimal.
items.e: 310 is 3 tenths. Tenths are the first place after the decimal point: 0.3.

items.q: Write 23100 as a decimal.
items.e: 23100 is 23 hundredths: 2 tenths and 3 hundredths. So the tenths digit is 2 and the hundredths digit is 3: 0.23.

items.q: Write 7100 as a decimal.
items.e: 7100 is 7 hundredths. Hundredths need two places after the point, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 0.07. (0.7 would be 7 tenths.)

items.q: Write 910 as a decimal.
items.e: 910 is 9 tenths. Tenths are the first place after the decimal point: 0.9.

items.q: Write 60100 as a decimal.
items.e: 60100 is 60 hundredths, which is the same as 6 tenths: 0.6 (or 0.60). 0.06 would be only 6 hundredths.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.4?
items.e: 0.4 has one digit after the point, so it means tenths: 4 tenths = 410. It is not 14: that is 0.25.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.09?
items.e: 0.09 has two digits after the point, so it means hundredths. The tenths digit is 0: 0.09 = 9 hundredths = 9100.

items.q: Which decimal is 4 tenths and 5 hundredths?
items.e: Tenths go in the first place after the point and hundredths in the second: 0.45.

items.q: Which decimal is 2 ones and 3 hundredths?
items.e: 2 ones, then the point. There are 0 tenths, so write a 0 before the 3 hundredths: 2.03. (2.3 would be 3 tenths.)

items.q: 1 whole is divided into 100 equal parts. What decimal is each part?
items.e: Each part is 1100 of the whole, one hundredth: 0.01. 0.1 is one tenth, which you get by dividing 1 into 10 parts.

items.q: 1 tenth is divided into 10 equal parts. What decimal is each part?
items.e: There are 10 tenths in 1 whole, and each tenth splits into 10 parts. That makes 10 × 10 = 100 parts in the whole, so each part is one hundredth: 0.01.

items.q: How many hundredths are there in 0.4?
items.e: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 4 tenths = 40 hundredths. 0.4 = 0.40. (4 is the number of tenths, not hundredths.)

sets.title: Halves, quarters and counting in hundredths

items.q: Write 12 as a decimal.
items.e: 12 = 510, because 5 is half of 10. So 12 = 0.5. Do not just write the 1 and the 2 as digits.

items.q: Write 14 as a decimal.
items.e: 14 of 100 is 25, so 14 = 25100 = 0.25. 0.4 is a common mistake: it uses the 4 from the bottom of the fraction.

items.q: Write 34 as a decimal.
items.e: 14 = 25 hundredths, so 34 = 3 × 25 = 75 hundredths = 0.75.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.25?
items.e: 0.25 = 25100. 25 is a quarter of 100, so 0.25 = 14.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.5?
items.e: 0.5 = 510 = 50 hundredths, which is half of 100. So 0.5 = 12. (15 is 0.2.)

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.75?
items.e: 0.75 = 75100. 75 is three quarters of 100, so 0.75 = 34.

items.q: What fraction of the hundred square is shaded?
items.e: 25 of the 100 squares are shaded: 25100 = 0.25. 4 lots of 25 make 100, so this is 14.

items.q: What fraction of the hundred square is shaded?
items.e: 75 of the 100 squares are shaded: 75100 = 0.75. Only 25 squares are white (14), so the shaded part is 34.

items.q:
Count up in hundredths. What comes next?
0.37, 0.38, 0.39, ?
items.e: 0.39 + 0.01: 9 hundredths and 1 more make 10 hundredths, which is 1 more tenth. So 3 tenths become 4 tenths: 0.40 (the same as 0.4). There is no such step as 0.310.

items.q:
Count down in hundredths. What comes next?
0.72, 0.71, 0.70, ?
items.e: 0.70 − 0.01: there are no hundredths left, so exchange 1 tenth for 10 hundredths. 7 tenths become 6 tenths and 9 hundredths: 0.69.

items.q:
Count up in hundredths. What comes next?
1.97, 1.98, 1.99, ?
items.e: 1.99 + 0.01: 99 hundredths and 1 more make 100 hundredths, which is 1 whole. So 1.99 + 0.01 = 2.00 (the same as 2).

items.q:
Count up in tenths. What comes next?
0.7, 0.8, 0.9, ?
items.e: 0.9 + 0.1: 9 tenths and 1 more make 10 tenths, which is 1 whole. So the next number is 1.0 (or 1). 0.10 is only 1 tenth.

items.q:
What is the missing number?
0.46, 0.47, ?, 0.49
items.e: The numbers go up by 1 hundredth each time: 0.47 + 0.01 = 0.48. Check: 0.48 + 0.01 = 0.49.

items.q: Start at 0.58. Count on 3 hundredths. Where do you land?
items.e: 0.59, 0.60, 0.61. After 0.59, 10 hundredths make a new tenth, so 0.59 + 0.01 = 0.60. You land on 0.61. (0.88 adds 3 tenths, not 3 hundredths.)

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: The line goes from 0.3 to 0.4, which is 1 tenth. It has 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth. 0.3 = 0.30. Count 6 spaces on: 0.36.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: The line goes from 0.8 to 0.9, which is 1 tenth. It has 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth. 0.8 = 0.80. Count 3 spaces on: 0.83.

items.q: The line from 0 to 1 is split into 4 equal parts. What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: 4 equal parts means each part is 14 = 0.25. The dot is 3 parts along: 34 = 0.75.

items.q: The line from 0 to 1 is split into 4 equal parts. What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: 4 equal parts means each part is 14. The dot is 1 part along: 14 = 0.25. It is not 0.1: the line has 4 parts, not 10.

items.q: Write 2 and 34 as a decimal.
items.e: 2 ones, then 34 = 0.75. So 2 and 34 = 2.75.

items.q: Write 1 and 14 as a decimal.
items.e: 1 one, then 14 = 0.25. So 1 and 14 = 1.25. (1.5 would be 1 and a half.)
Dividing by 10 makes the number 10 times smaller. Each digit moves 1 place to the right: 7 ÷ 10 = 0.7. Write a 0 in the ones place.
Dividing by 10 makes the number 10 times smaller. Each digit moves 1 place to the right: 3 ÷ 10 = 0.3. Write a 0 in the ones place.
Dividing by 100 makes the number 100 times smaller. Each digit moves 2 places to the right: 4 ÷ 100 = 0.04. Write a 0 in the ones place (and in the tenths place).
Dividing by 100 makes the number 100 times smaller. Each digit moves 2 places to the right: 8 ÷ 100 = 0.08. Write a 0 in the ones place (and in the tenths place).
Dividing by 10 makes the number 10 times smaller. Each digit moves 1 place to the right: 34 ÷ 10 = 3.4.
Dividing by 10 makes the number 10 times smaller. Each digit moves 1 place to the right: 56 ÷ 10 = 5.6.
Dividing by 10 makes the number 10 times smaller. Each digit moves 1 place to the right: 82 ÷ 10 = 8.2.
Dividing by 10 makes the number 10 times smaller. Each digit moves 1 place to the right: 60 ÷ 10 = 6. The ones digit 0 moves to the tenths place, so 6.0 is just 6.
Dividing by 100 makes the number 100 times smaller. Each digit moves 2 places to the right: 27 ÷ 100 = 0.27. Write a 0 in the ones place.
Dividing by 100 makes the number 100 times smaller. Each digit moves 2 places to the right: 75 ÷ 100 = 0.75. Write a 0 in the ones place.
Dividing by 100 makes the number 100 times smaller. Each digit moves 2 places to the right: 20 ÷ 100 = 0.2. Write a 0 in the ones place. 0.20 is the same as 0.2.
Dividing by 100 makes the number 100 times smaller. Each digit moves 2 places to the right: 61 ÷ 100 = 0.61. Write a 0 in the ones place.

items.q: The chart shows 47 ÷ 10 = 4.7. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 47 ÷ 10 = 4.7. The digits moved 1 place to the right, so the 7 is now in the tenths place. Its value is 7 tenths.

items.q: The chart shows 58 ÷ 100 = 0.58. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 58 ÷ 100 = 0.58. The digits moved 2 places to the right, so the 8 is now in the hundredths place. Its value is 8 hundredths.

items.q: The chart shows 36 ÷ 10 = 3.6. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 36 ÷ 10 = 3.6. The digits moved 1 place to the right, so the 3 is now in the ones place. Its value is 3 ones.

items.q: The chart shows 90 ÷ 100 = 0.9. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 90 ÷ 100 = 0.9. The digits moved 2 places to the right, so the 9 is now in the tenths place. Its value is 9 tenths.

items.q: Which calculation has the answer 0.38?
items.e: 0.38 is 38 hundredths. Dividing 38 by 100 moves both digits 2 places to the right: 38 ÷ 100 = 0.38. 38 ÷ 10 is 3.8.
8 ÷ 10 = 0.8. Then 0.8 ÷ 10 = 0.08. Dividing by 10 twice is the same as dividing by 100.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: The ones are the same, so compare the tenths: 4 tenths and 5 tenths. So 0.45 < 0.54. The tenths decide it, not the last digit.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: The ones are the same, so compare the tenths: 7 tenths and 2 tenths. So 3.7 > 3.2.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: The ones are the same, so compare the tenths: 0 tenths and 8 tenths. So 0.08 < 0.80. The tenths decide it, not the last digit.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: The ones are the same, so compare the tenths: 6 tenths and 3 tenths. So 2.63 > 2.36. The tenths decide it, not the last digit.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Compare the ones first: 5.1 has 5 ones and 4.9 has 4 ones, so 5.1 > 4.9.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: The ones are the same, so compare the tenths: 7 tenths and 1 tenth. So 0.71 > 0.17. The tenths decide it, not the last digit.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: The ones and tenths are the same, so compare the hundredths: 8 and 3. So 6.48 > 6.43.

items.q: Which decimal is the greatest?
items.e: All have 0 ones. Compare the tenths: 0.83 and 0.80 both have 8 tenths. Then the hundredths: 3 > 0. So 0.83 is the greatest.

items.q: Which decimal is the smallest?
items.e: Compare the ones first: 2.4 and 2.9 have 2 ones. Then the tenths: 4 < 9. So 2.4 is the smallest.

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare the tenths: 0.05 has 0, 0.35 has 3 and 0.53 has 5. So the order is 0.05, 0.35, 0.53.

items.q: Round 4.6 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 4.6 is between 4 and 5. Look at the tenths digit: 6. 5 or more rounds up, so 4.6 rounds to 5.

items.q: Round 4.5 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 4.5 is between 4 and 5. Look at the tenths digit: 5. 5 or more rounds up, so 4.5 rounds to 5. 4.5 is exactly halfway: halfway always rounds up.

items.q: Round 7.2 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 7.2 is between 7 and 8. Look at the tenths digit: 2. 4 or less rounds down, so 7.2 rounds to 7.

items.q: Round 12.8 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 12.8 is between 12 and 13. Look at the tenths digit: 8. 5 or more rounds up, so 12.8 rounds to 13.

items.q: Round 0.7 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 0.7 is between 0 and 1. Look at the tenths digit: 7. 5 or more rounds up, so 0.7 rounds to 1.

items.q: Round 9.5 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 9.5 is between 9 and 10. Look at the tenths digit: 5. 5 or more rounds up, so 9.5 rounds to 10. Halfway always rounds up.

items.q: Round 6.1 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 6.1 is between 6 and 7. Look at the tenths digit: 1. 4 or less rounds down, so 6.1 rounds to 6.

items.q: The red dot shows 2.3. What is 2.3 rounded to the nearest whole number?
items.e: The dot is between 2 and 3. It is before the halfway mark (2.5), so it is nearer to 2.

items.q: The red dot shows 15.7. What is 15.7 rounded to the nearest whole number?
items.e: The dot is between 15 and 16. It is past the halfway mark (15.5), so it is nearer to 16. The tenths digit is 7, and 5 or more rounds up.

items.q: Which number rounds to 6 to the nearest whole number?
items.e: 5.7 has 7 tenths, so it rounds up to 6. 5.4 rounds down to 5. 6.5 and 6.7 round up to 7.

items.q: A pencil costs 45p. How do you write 45p in pounds?
items.e: There are 100p in £1, so 1p = £0.01. 45p = 45100 of £1 = £0.45. (£4.50 is 450p.)

items.q: A comic costs £3.70. How many pence is that?
items.e: £3 = 300p and 70p more: 300p + 70p = 370p. The 7 is 7 tenths of a pound, which is 70p.

items.q: Freya has £2.45. Her gran gives her £1. How much money does she have now?
items.e: Add £1 to the pounds: £2 + £1 = £3. The pence stay the same: £3.45. (£2.46 adds 1p, not £1.)

items.q: Alfie has £5.60. He spends £2.30 on a book. How much money does he have left?
items.e: Subtract pounds from pounds and pence from pence: £5 − £2 = £3 and 60p − 30p = 30p. So Alfie has £3.30 left.

items.q: Poppy has a ribbon 1.25 m long and another ribbon 0.5 m long. How long are they altogether?
items.e: 0.5 m = 0.50 m. Add tenths to tenths and hundredths to hundredths: 1.25 + 0.50 = 1.75 m. (1.30 m comes from adding the 5 to the hundredths.)

items.q: Leo runs 100 m in 15.7 seconds. What is his time to the nearest second?
items.e: 15.7 is between 15 and 16. The tenths digit is 7, so round up: 16 seconds.

items.q: In the long jump, Isla jumps 2.48 m and George jumps 2.84 m. Who jumps further?
items.e: Both jumps are 2 whole metres. Compare the tenths: 2.84 has 8 tenths and 2.48 has 4 tenths. So George jumps further.

items.q: A melon has a mass of 2.6 kg. What is its mass to the nearest kilogram?
items.e: 2.6 is between 2 and 3. The tenths digit is 6, so round up: 3 kg.

items.q: Kai cuts a 1 m stick in half. How long is each piece in metres?
items.e: Half of 1 m is 12 m = 510 m = 0.5 m (50 cm).

items.q: A jug holds 14 of a litre of milk. Write this as a decimal.
items.e: 14 = 25100 = 0.25. So the jug holds 0.25 litres (250 ml).

items.q: How much is 34 of £1?
items.e: £1 = 100p. 14 of 100p is 25p, so 34 of 100p is 3 × 25p = 75p (£0.75). 25p is only 14.

items.q: Grace’s pencil is 14 cm long. 1 cm is 1100 of a metre. How long is the pencil in metres?
items.e: 14 cm = 14100 m. To change cm to m, divide by 100: 14 ÷ 100 = 0.14 m. (1.4 m would be 140 cm.)

items.q: £7 is shared equally between 10 children. How much does each child get?
items.e: £7 ÷ 10 = £0.70. The 7 moves 1 place to the right, into the tenths place. £0.70 = 70p. (7p would be £7 ÷ 100.)

items.q: A rope 3 m long is cut into 10 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 3 ÷ 10 = 0.3 m (30 cm). Dividing by 10 moves the 3 one place to the right, into the tenths place.

items.q: A ball costs £3.45 and a kite costs £3.54. Which is cheaper?
items.e: Both cost £3 and some pence. Compare the tenths: 4 tenths (40p) is less than 5 tenths (50p). £3.45 < £3.54, so the ball is cheaper.

items.q: A sunflower is 0.98 m tall. It grows 0.02 m more. How tall is it now?
items.e: Count on 2 hundredths: 0.99, 1.00. 100 hundredths make 1 whole, so the sunflower is 1.00 m (1 m) tall.

items.q: Lily’s school bag has a mass of 3.5 kg. What is that to the nearest kilogram?
items.e: 3.5 is exactly halfway between 3 and 4. Halfway rounds up, so the answer is 4 kg.

items.q: A water bottle holds 0.75 litres. Which fraction of a litre is that?
c: 14 of a litre
7510 of a litre
34 of a litre
75 of a litre
items.e: 0.75 = 75100. 75 is three quarters of 100, so the bottle holds 34 of a litre (750 ml).

items.q: On sports day, Zara runs the race in 12.4 seconds and Jack runs it in 12.9 seconds. Who is faster?
items.e: In a race, the shorter time is faster. 12.4 < 12.9, because 4 tenths < 9 tenths. So Zara is faster.

items.q: Mohammed has a £1 coin, a 50p coin, a 20p coin and a 5p coin. How much money is that?
items.e: 50p + 20p + 5p = 75p. Then £1 + 75p = £1.75. (£76 comes from adding 1 + 50 + 20 + 5, but the £1 coin is 100p, not 1p.)
